findings.title: No re-check of cache after acquiring write lock
findings.body: After the read-lock fast path fails, the function takes the write lock but never re-reads entryPointAssetsCache. If N requests arrive concurrently on a cold cache, each one in turn will re-read and re-parse assets-manifest.json (or hit the CDN) while serialized on the mutex, instead of the first filling the cache and the rest returning it. Re-checking `entryPointAssetsCache != nil` (for non-Dev env) right after Lock() avoids the redundant I/O and the resulting latency spike at startup.

findings.title: Failed load overwrites a previously valid cached value with nil
findings.body: `entryPointAssetsCache = result` is executed unconditionally, including when readWebAssetsFromFile/CDN returned an error and result is nil. A single transient failure (e.g. file temporarily unreadable, CDN error) wipes an already-good cached value, so every subsequent call must reload and will return nil assets until a load succeeds. The assignment should be guarded by `if err == nil && result != nil`.
